About The Role

What if your native German fluency could help teach AI how to handle a real phone call to a doctor's office? We're looking for native German speakers based in the New York area to hold natural spoken conversations with an AI healthcare receptionist, then evaluate how well it listens, responds, and takes action.

New York's large German-speaking community — from recent expats to heritage speakers — makes it an ideal place to find people with the authentic, natural German speech this project demands. You'll role-play as a patient using fictional personas we provide, record short conversations, and grade the AI's performance.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role for people with clear German speech, strong attention to detail, and an ear for what sounds natural and fluent.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Contract (task-based)
Location: Remote

We are now accepting applications for the Genentech 2027 Summer Internship Program in Development Sciences (DevSci); this post is for a computational biology role in Translational Safety (TS). Translational Safety is an integral part of DevSci. We contribute to the organization’s success by providing scientific insights and ensuring the safety of molecules that advance through the pipeline to patients. We do this to support the DevSci vision to deliver the right drug in the right dose to the right patient. We are also committed to providing better outcomes for our people, patients, business, and communities by advancing and boldly championing diversity, equity, and inclusion in our work.

The selected candidate will use dose-resolved single-cell RNA-seq data to model how cell populations respond to chemical perturbations. The intern will benchmark foundation models alongside other computational approaches for capturing dose-dependent responses and predicting the effects of previously unseen compounds. The project will also compare in vitro perturbation states with relevant in vivo cellular programs to identify response features that are most informative for human-relevant toxicology.

This internship position is located in South San Francisco, on-site.

Model perturbation responses: Develop and benchmark computational approaches to capture reproducible, dose-dependent cellular responses.
Test generalization: Evaluate whether learned response patterns can predict the effects of compounds not used during model development.

Assess translational relevance: Compare in vitro perturbation signatures with relevant in vivo cellular programs to evaluate their relevance for human safety.

Intensive 12-weeks, full-time (40 hours per week) paid internship.

jobs.description:
Job Description

The mission of the UCSF Department of Surgery is threefold: to develop the next generation of leaders in surgery; to provide outstanding quality clinical care that is cost effective, yet compassionate; and to make significant advances in scientific knowledge and clinical practice through basic and clinical research. Care of patients is what attracted our faculty and residents to surgery, and it continues to be our main focus. The Department is comprised of seven divisions including Adult Cardiothoracic Surgery, General Surgery, Pediatric Cardiothoracic Surgery, Pediatric Surgery, Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery, Transplant Surgery, and Vascular & Endovascular Surgery.

The UCSF-ITL is a high complexity clinical laboratory that performs tests and provides services that support solid organ (kidney, heart, lung, liver, pancreas, islet, etc.) and hematopoietic stem cell (blood, marrow, cord blood, etc.) transplant programs. The laboratory is CLIA certified and is licensed by the states of California and New York. The lab is also certified as a free-standing-histocompatibility laboratory by the Centers of Medicare and Medicaid (CMS). The laboratory serves as a core laboratory for the NIH Immune Tolerance Network and provides support for several national clinical trials.

Perform laboratory functions that support solid organ and blood & marrow transplant programs. Functions include on-call responsibilities for the deceased donor transplant programs; perform infectious disease testing; data entry of patient and sample information into various systems, prepare cell subsets; isolate DNA; HLA type by various methods; crossmatch by flow cytometry method; test and identify HLA antibodies; chimerism monitoring and other HLA-related tests; assist in managing samples (store, retrieve, and aliquot samples); perform quality control and routine maintenance of various laboratory equipment; analyze and report laboratory data; order supplies, repairs, and other services; answer phones and perform other duties as assigned.

Tidy and orderly

jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

Here at Jacobs, we apply our expertise and knowledge as we look into the future with great optimism and focus. We don’t settle until we give our best and know that we’re making a difference.

We're seeking to hire an CSA
Walkdown/Turnover SME
for an onsite role at our data center project in Saint Francisville, LA
.

As a Civil, Structural, and Architectural Walkdown/Turnover Subject Matter Expert
, you will be responsible for coordinating and facilitating the field verification and documentation of civil, structural, and architectural work installed by Construction.

You will provide technical leadership during CSA walkdowns on an active construction site, guiding construction, subcontractor, field Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client personnel through defined areas, structures, buildings, rooms, equipment-support scopes, and facility boundaries.

You will collaborate with field Quality and CSA subcontractors to verify adherence to applicable inspection, testing, completion, and turnover-documentation requirements. The position will focus on confirming that permanent facilities are sufficiently complete to safely support equipment installation, system testing, startup, commissioning, occupancy, access, weather protection, and final turnover.

You will use ACC for CSA punch-list entry and tracking, condition documentation, readiness visibility, closure review, and assembly of applicable construction turnover packages.

In coordination with Project Controls and Construction, you will help provide a planned and documented approach for the turnover of civil, structural, and architectural scopes in alignment with the P6 schedule and downstream system dependencies.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and facilitate CSA walkdowns with Construction, subcontractors, Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client representatives.
Serve as the primary CSA technical resource for walkdown preparation, field verification, punch development, and turnover-package review.
Confirm that each CSA walkdown has a clearly defined building, area, room, structure, foundation, or facility boundary.
Participate with Construction and CQV in establishing logical completion and turnover boundaries that support equipment installation, system turnover, startup, and commissioning.
Read and interpret civil and grading plans, underground utility and drainage drawings, concrete and foundation drawings, structural steel drawings, architectural plans, building sections, roofing details, door and hardware schedules, finish schedules, firestopping details, and equipment-foundation drawings.
Verify roads, paving, grading, drainage, concrete foundations and slabs, structural steel, access systems, building envelopes, roofing, walls, ceilings, doors, firestopping, finishes, equipment clearances, egress, and permanent safety features against approved scope.
Review the availability and traceability of survey and as-built records, soil compaction records, concrete placement and strength records, anchor-bolt and embed records, structural bolting records, welding and NDE records, coating records, roofing and waterproofing records, and firestopping inspection records.
Identify conditions that could affect safety, access, weather-tightness, fire rating, equipment installation, system testing, startup, commissioning, or facility turnover.
Enter and track CSA punch-list items in CxAlloy using clear descriptions of the exact location, observed condition, affected scope, and required correction.
Coordinate with Construction and field Quality to resolve issues and support assignment of punch ownership and target dates.
Review submitted closure evidence and coordinate reinspection when required.
Review CSA turnover packages for completeness, organization, traceability, and alignment with the defined scope.
Coordinate CSA readiness forecasts with the P6 schedule, equipment-installation milestones, access requirements, weather-tightness needs, and downstream testing activities.
Identify temporary conditions or incomplete permanent work that could affect system turnover or construction-to-CQV handoff.
Participate in CSA readiness reviews, turnover planning, construction-completion discussions, and facility handoff activities.
Promote a positive, collaborative, and problem-solving culture among project participants.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience in lieu of a degree.
At least 5 years of civil, structural, architectural, Quality, inspection, or turnover experience, including at least 2 years supporting walkdowns, systems completion, or facility turnover.
Experience on data center, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial, power, commercial, or other major capital projects.
Ability to lead CSA walkdowns with subcontractors, Quality personnel, CQV representatives, and clients.
Ability to read and interpret civil, structural, architectural, concrete, steel, roofing, and equipment-foundation drawings.
Knowledge of CSA inspection, testing, completion, and turnover-documentation requirements and their relationship to downstream readiness.
Strong organization, issue tracking, field documentation, and communication skills.
Ability to spend continuous hours on an active construction site and remain onsite for the duration of the assignment.

Experience with CxAlloy and Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC).
Familiarity with Good Documentation Practices and P6 turnover milestone planning.
Working knowledge of ACI, AISC, AWS, ICC, NFPA, firestopping, roofing, or coating requirements.
Experience with data-center buildings, substations, equipment yards, concrete foundations, structural steel, roofing, fire-rated assemblies, and mission-critical facilities.

Idaho National Laboratory’s (INL) Materials and Fuels Complex is seeking forward-thinking professionals interested in exploring a career as a Nuclear Facility Research Technician.

The Materials and Fuels Complex (MFC) is seeking nuclear facility research technicians. MFC is hiring for multiple facilities with multiple shift opportunities.

Department Overview

This position provides technical support in the Transfusion Services to complete laboratory testing for OHSU

hospital and clinic patients. The incumbent will be a qualified Medical Laboratory Technician with generalist

experience or equivalent capable of performing laboratory testing and associated activities needed to support

the technical services provided by the Transfusion Services. This position will require testing skills in

Transfusion Service. Testing is performed in Transfusion Services suing the Grifols Erytra and manual testing

processes utilizing both gel and tube. This position will also have some limited testing responsibilities in the

Core Lab. Specimen processing, test performance, and result reporting is performed independently after

appropriate training. Additional review of results is required in the case of unusual/complex results,

procedural problems, or when dictated by policy or procedure. The person filling this position will be of

professional demeanor and perform their duties with an attitude, which will best serve the clients of the

department.

Function/Duties of Position

Medical Laboratory Technician Testing Duties

Perform routine lab testing; accurately record results and interpretations by computer entry and/or legibly in writing.
Use lab instruments to include the Grifols Erytra. Utilize supplies and equipment responsibly and according to lab and manufacturer's guidelines and Transfusion Service procedures.
Perform gel and manual serologic testing to resolve problems encountered in routine testing, accurately record results and interpretations.
Follow established policies and procedures but obtain consult to resolve complex issues; bring to the attention of the Medical Laboratory Scientists, Technical Coordinator, Manager, or Medical Director. Seek guidance from or notify the Technical Coordinator, Manager, Medical Director, or Resident, when appropriate.

Medical Laboratory Technician Product Bench Duties

Recognize incorrect or unusual blood product orders and take steps to modify the order after consult with patient physician or Transfusion Service medical staff or resident.
Maintain and manage an adequate inventory of perishable blood products and ensure that excessive wastage does not occur.
Choose appropriate blood products for patients based on urgency of need, available inventory, lab results, and therapeutic requirements.
Prepare blood components; document preparation, and label according to SOP. Thaw plasma and cryoprecipitate; irradiate blood products, divide blood products into aliquots using correct technique; pool blood products.
Properly issue blood products and document issue/inspection manually and in HCLL. Receive and document returned blood products to inventory; quarantine as appropriate.
Sign in blood products received from Red Cross with appropriate documentation. Issue and receive blood products to and from patient care areas.
Document transactions involving blood products correctly and legibly, i.e., receive/issue documentation; verbal orders; and orders placed with Red Cross, etc.

Quality Control Monitoring, Maintenance and Review

Perform Quality control, periodic maintenance and Proficiency Testing as assigned.
Perform and document maintenance of analyzers, blood storage and other equipment. Troubleshoot equipment and interact with vendors, as needed.
Participate in departmental Quality Monitoring/Improvement processes. Recognize and document variations, errors, and accidents.
Document proper temperature of blood products in transit from hospital to hospital, and internally at OHSU.
Inspect blood products for appropriate appearance. Organize, check for accuracy, and report blood product usage statistics as assigned.
Maintain inventory of supplies and ordering; alert Technical Coordinator or Manager when supplies are low in a timely manner.
Accurately bill blood products and testing, and record audit trail of product use in compliance with regulatory and accrediting requirements.

Other Duties As Assigned

Required Qualifications

Completion of a 2 year accredited program in Medical Laboratory Technician training plus MLT (ASCP) within 90 days of hire or AMT certification within 90 days of hire. Depending on date of training, different continuing education requirements will apply. OR
Bachelor’s degree in a chemical or biological science and two years of Laboratory Technical Assistant training/experience performing standardized laboratory tests in the specialty area(s) in which high complexity testing will be performed; MLT (ASCP) or AMT certification preferred. Depending on date of training, different continuing education requirements will apply.

Job Related Knowledge, Skills And Abilities (Competencies)

General knowledge of laboratory terminology, equipment, materials and techniques, regulations and safety.
Skill in handling of laboratory specimens, record keeping and laboratory equipment.
Skill in identifying cells and cell morphology.
Skill in using several different computer systems, including: word processing, dedicated LIS/HIS, etc.
Ability to follow written and oral instructions accurately, and operate and maintain standard laboratory equipment.
Ability to work independently within established guidelines, to adjust to rapidly changing priorities, and apply problem-solving skills.
Ability to demonstrate performance of job duties to trainees.
Demonstrate personal integrity, efficiency, and ability to adjust to rapidly changing testing priorities.
Ability to work in a multi-tasking environment and display technical skills at many different workstations throughout the laboratory.

Preferred Qualifications

Generalist experience in Transfusion Services within last two years preferred.

Additional Details

Positions in the laboratory and environs may require working flexible schedules including nights weekends

and holidays; working at multiple laboratory or hospital sites; traveling between laboratories and sites by

stairs, elevator, tram, shuttle or other means; exposure to blood and body fluids, chemical hazards,

radiation; working in a somewhat noisy and crowded environment; wearing gloves and other Personal

Protective Equipment for long periods of time; experiencing occasional temperature control problems in

building.

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

Here at Jacobs, we apply our expertise and knowledge as we look into the future with great optimism and focus. We don’t settle until we give our best and know that we’re making a difference.

We're seeking to hire an CSA
Walkdown/Turnover SME
for an onsite role at our data center project in Saint Francisville, LA
.

As a Civil, Structural, and Architectural Walkdown/Turnover Subject Matter Expert
, you will be responsible for coordinating and facilitating the field verification and documentation of civil, structural, and architectural work installed by Construction.

You will provide technical leadership during CSA walkdowns on an active construction site, guiding construction, subcontractor, field Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client personnel through defined areas, structures, buildings, rooms, equipment-support scopes, and facility boundaries.

You will collaborate with field Quality and CSA subcontractors to verify adherence to applicable inspection, testing, completion, and turnover-documentation requirements. The position will focus on confirming that permanent facilities are sufficiently complete to safely support equipment installation, system testing, startup, commissioning, occupancy, access, weather protection, and final turnover.

You will use ACC for CSA punch-list entry and tracking, condition documentation, readiness visibility, closure review, and assembly of applicable construction turnover packages.

In coordination with Project Controls and Construction, you will help provide a planned and documented approach for the turnover of civil, structural, and architectural scopes in alignment with the P6 schedule and downstream system dependencies.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and facilitate CSA walkdowns with Construction, subcontractors, Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client representatives.
Serve as the primary CSA technical resource for walkdown preparation, field verification, punch development, and turnover-package review.
Confirm that each CSA walkdown has a clearly defined building, area, room, structure, foundation, or facility boundary.
Participate with Construction and CQV in establishing logical completion and turnover boundaries that support equipment installation, system turnover, startup, and commissioning.
Read and interpret civil and grading plans, underground utility and drainage drawings, concrete and foundation drawings, structural steel drawings, architectural plans, building sections, roofing details, door and hardware schedules, finish schedules, firestopping details, and equipment-foundation drawings.
Verify roads, paving, grading, drainage, concrete foundations and slabs, structural steel, access systems, building envelopes, roofing, walls, ceilings, doors, firestopping, finishes, equipment clearances, egress, and permanent safety features against approved scope.
Review the availability and traceability of survey and as-built records, soil compaction records, concrete placement and strength records, anchor-bolt and embed records, structural bolting records, welding and NDE records, coating records, roofing and waterproofing records, and firestopping inspection records.
Identify conditions that could affect safety, access, weather-tightness, fire rating, equipment installation, system testing, startup, commissioning, or facility turnover.
Enter and track CSA punch-list items in CxAlloy using clear descriptions of the exact location, observed condition, affected scope, and required correction.
Coordinate with Construction and field Quality to resolve issues and support assignment of punch ownership and target dates.
Review submitted closure evidence and coordinate reinspection when required.
Review CSA turnover packages for completeness, organization, traceability, and alignment with the defined scope.
Coordinate CSA readiness forecasts with the P6 schedule, equipment-installation milestones, access requirements, weather-tightness needs, and downstream testing activities.
Identify temporary conditions or incomplete permanent work that could affect system turnover or construction-to-CQV handoff.
Participate in CSA readiness reviews, turnover planning, construction-completion discussions, and facility handoff activities.
Promote a positive, collaborative, and problem-solving culture among project participants.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience in lieu of a degree.
At least 5 years of civil, structural, architectural, Quality, inspection, or turnover experience, including at least 2 years supporting walkdowns, systems completion, or facility turnover.
Experience on data center, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial, power, commercial, or other major capital projects.
Ability to lead CSA walkdowns with subcontractors, Quality personnel, CQV representatives, and clients.
Ability to read and interpret civil, structural, architectural, concrete, steel, roofing, and equipment-foundation drawings.
Knowledge of CSA inspection, testing, completion, and turnover-documentation requirements and their relationship to downstream readiness.
Strong organization, issue tracking, field documentation, and communication skills.
Ability to spend continuous hours on an active construction site and remain onsite for the duration of the assignment.

Ideally, You'll Also Have

Experience with CxAlloy and Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC).
Familiarity with Good Documentation Practices and P6 turnover milestone planning.
Working knowledge of ACI, AISC, AWS, ICC, NFPA, firestopping, roofing, or coating requirements.
Experience with data-center buildings, substations, equipment yards, concrete foundations, structural steel, roofing, fire-rated assemblies, and mission-critical facilities.
OSHA 30
Relevant ACI, ICC, AWS-CWI, firestop, coating, or construction-inspection certification.

Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

Qualified applicants with criminal histories will be considered for employment

Join Amgens Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like youre part of something bigger, its because you are. Our shared missionto serve patients living with serious illnessesdrives all that we do.

Since 1980, weve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the worlds toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, youll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, youll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Civil Engineer

What you will do

Lets do this. Lets change the world. In this vital role you will provide technical leadership and engineering expertise for the planning, design, renovation, and delivery of civil and structural infrastructure supporting facilities, utilities, and capital projects. This role ensures designs are safe, compliant, constructible, reliable, and aligned with operational, business, and site requirements.

The Project Engineer partners with engineering disciplines, architects, project managers, facilities teams, EHS professionals, contractors, and external design firms throughout the project lifecycle. This position requires travel to project sites and organizational locations to support project development, design reviews, field assessments, construction activities, commissioning, and stakeholder engagement.

Serve as the technical lead for civil and structural engineering requirements, design standards, specifications, and project execution.

Develop and review civil and structural design criteria, calculations, drawings, specifications, scopes of work, and engineering studies.

Support projects involving site development, grading, drainage, stormwater management, roads, parking areas, underground utilities, foundations, structural steel, concrete, and building modifications.

Evaluate existing site and structural conditions; identify constraints, risks, and required remediation or reinforcement measures.

Review engineering design packages for technical quality, code compliance, constructability, maintainability, safety, and alignment with project requirements.

Coordinate with architectural, mechanical, electrical, process, environmental, and facility engineering disciplines to ensure integrated project solutions.

Lead technical aspects of capital projects from feasibility and concept development through detailed design, construction, commissioning, and turnover.

Travel as needed to support site assessments, project meetings, design workshops, construction reviews, inspections, commissioning, and operational-readiness activities.

Provide technical support during construction, including field observations, resolution of design issues, review of contractor submittals, and evaluation of change requests.

Ensure projects comply with applicable building codes, structural standards, civil design requirements, permitting obligations, and environmental regulations.

Support the development and maintenance of civil and structural engineering standards, specifications, guidelines, and standard details.

Identify design risks, recommend practical mitigations, and support risk assessments associated with facility modifications, infrastructure reliability, and site conditions.

Support commissioning and turnover activities to confirm civil and structural systems meet intended-use and operational requirements.

Monitor industry practices, codes, standards, and emerging technologies; incorporate relevant improvements into engineering standards and project delivery practices.

Provide technical mentoring and subject matter support to project teams and less-experienced engineers.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is a leader with these qualifications.

Basic Qualifications

Doctorate degree

OR

Masters degree and 2 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

OR

Bachelors degree and 4 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

OR

Associates degree and 8 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

OR

High school diploma / GED and 10 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

Preferred Qualifications

Professional Engineer (PE) license in civil or structural engineering.

Advanced degree in civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related discipline.

Experience supporting industrial, manufacturing, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, research, or other regulated facility environments.

Experience with structural assessments, seismic evaluations, existing-building modifications, and infrastructure renewal projects.

Familiarity with stormwater management, site permitting, geotechnical engineering, and construction-phase engineering support.

Experience with relevant engineering software for structural analysis, civil design, or site-development planning.

What you can expect from us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, well support your journey every step of the way.
